name: Kate Ristau

bio.statement: Ristau's pamphlet statement lists Tigard Library Board service from 2017 to present, as chair from 2022 to present.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Tigard Library Board (2017–Present), Chair (2022–Present)

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)

bio.statement: The pamphlet describes Ristau as a nonprofit executive, community leader, 20-plus-year Tigard resident and parent.
bio.excerpt: Kate is a nonprofit executive, community leader, 20+ year Tigard resident, and a mom.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)

bio.statement: Her campaign website describes her as a community leader, nonprofit executive and chair of the Tigard Library Board.
bio.excerpt: Kate Ristau is a Tigard community leader, nonprofit executive, and Chair of the Tigard Library Board.

positions.statement: Ristau's pamphlet statement lists responsible planning as a priority, including budget decisions reflecting community values and protecting taxpayer dollars.
positions.excerpt: PLAN RESPONSIBLY by making smart budget decisions that reflect our community’s values, protecting taxpayer dollars, and investing in strong city services.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement prioritizes the Tigard Public Library, recreation programs and ensuring every child in Tigard has enough to eat.
positions.excerpt: PROTECT COMMUNITY SERVICES by investing in the Tigard Public Library, funding recreation programs, and working to ensure every child in Tigard has enough to eat.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement supports encouraging starter homes and workforce housing, with land use decisions from the Tigard Triangle to River Terrace 2.0.
positions.excerpt: SUPPORT HOUSING WE CAN AFFORD by encouraging starter homes, workforce housing, and smart land use decisions from the Tigard Triangle to River Terrace 2.0.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists improving transportation and sidewalks on Hall Boulevard, Highway 99W and SW 72nd Avenue, and investing in parks, trails and public spaces.
positions.excerpt: MAKE TIGARD SAFER AND MORE CONNECTED by improving transportation and sidewalks on Hall Boulevard, Highway 99W, and SW 72nd Avenue

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement supports investing in downtown Tigard, supporting local businesses and streamlining permitting.
positions.excerpt: SUPPORT A THRIVING LOCAL ECONOMY by investing in downtown Tigard, supporting local businesses, and streamlining permitting to make it easier to do business in Tigard.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-39)
